rationale: The stripping algebra is internally correct (adding Δ noncash CA removes liquidation boosts, subtracting Δ operating liabilities removes stretch financing) and the sign is coherent, but neutralizing both working-capital legs turns leg two into something close to accrual-free cash earnings, which is highly collinear with the oibdp/at leg and risks degenerating the MIN interaction into a plain profitability sort.

This is a cosmetic MA(3) smoothing of the already-evaluated "Operating Margin Working Capital Turnover" (fmb 3.23, ls_talpha 2.65) with the same two legs and same mechanism, so it is a near-rediscovery rather than a substantive refinement.

Substituting the change in noncash-current-asset intensity for the archived level/TS_RANK leg is a genuine flow-vs-stock distinction and the sign is consistent, but it sits close to both "Gross Margin Lean Operating Cycle" and "Margin Expansion Asset Discipline" and therefore offers only modest incremental information.

The construction is internally consistent (NEG of SG&A-intensity trend correctly encodes cost discipline as a high value) and the lean-cycle conditioner is a fresh pairing, though the SG&A-trend leg has repeatedly delivered null or wrong-signed portfolio evidence in this archive, so prior odds are unfavorable.

This is the most substantively motivated proposal — it explicitly reconciles the conflicting asset-side and liability-side working-capital legs into a single coherent cash-conversion conditioner with correct signs — though the liability leg's previously negative Fama-MacBeth slope against a positive prior means the two SUMRANK components may partially offset in the cross-section.

Sign and construction line up (high margin times falling turnover yields a large positive signal expected to predict negatively) and the deterioration channel is distinct from the turnover-level signal, but the first difference of an unbounded sale/(act−che) ratio is a noisy, scale-unstable quantity that 1% winsorization may not adequately tame.
